title: DNS Latency Degradation by Resolver
dataSources: UniFi controller events (`unifi:event`), Pi-hole query log (`pihole:query`), AdGuard Home (`adguard:query`), speedtest-cli results (`speedtest:result`), router/firewall syslog, ISP uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: UniFi / router syslog, Pi-hole/AdGuard, and scheduled speedtests via HEC scripted inputs and the Universal Forwarder.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=pihole:query
| bin _time span=1h
| stats avg(reply_time_ms) as avg_ms by upstream _time
| eventstats avg(avg_ms) as baseline by upstream
| where avg_ms>baseline*1.5 AND avg_ms>50
| sort - avg_ms
description: Compares hourly DNS response time against each upstream resolver's own baseline and catches the nameserver that is suddenly making everything feel slow.
value: Slow DNS harms the whole home network in subtle ways; a resolver-specific trend gives you a quick answer before blaming the ISP or Wi-Fi.
implementation: Forward Pi-hole query timing and upstream server fields; alert when one resolver drifts materially above normal latency.
visualization: Hourly table of upstream resolvers by average response time and baseline delta.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks which DNS server is suddenly taking much longer than usual to answer lookups for your home devices.
